The problem is that there's a local `yaml.py` file in the project directory that shadows the real `yaml` (PyYAML) library. When `orders/service.py` does `import yaml`, Python imports the local `yaml.py` instead of the installed PyYAML package, and the local file doesn't have a `dump` function.

All tests pass. The root cause was that a local file named `yaml.py` was shadowing the installed PyYAML library. When `orders/service.py` did `import yaml`, Python imported the local `yaml.py` (which only contained project notes) instead of the real PyYAML package, causing `yaml.dump({})` to fail with `AttributeError: module 'yaml' has no attribute 'dump'`. The fix was to rename `yaml.py` to `project_notes.py` so it no longer shadows the `yaml` package.
